mainTopic: The separate powers of חכם and בעל over vows, the גזירה שוה of 'זה הדבר' between נדרים and שחוטי חוץ, and how בית שמאי, who reject it, learn their laws
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא that reads 'זה הדבר' to teach that only a חכם does התרה. A second ברייתא teaches that only a בעל does הפרה, even though a קל וחומר might have given that power to the חכם too. A third ברייתא links פרשת נדרים and שחוטי חוץ through a גזירה שוה on 'זה הדבר'. From this link, רב אחא בר יעקב learns that three הדיוטות can release a vow, and רב חסדא (or רבי יוחנן) learns that one יחיד מומחה can also do it. רב ששת learns from the other direction of the link that שאלה works on הקדש. Since בית שמאי hold there is no שאלה on הקדש, the גמרא says they do not accept this גזירה שוה at all. For them, each 'זה הדבר' teaches its own local law. They learn the law of three הדיוטות from the answer רב ששת gave רב אסי בר נתן about a ברייתא saying שבת and vows were not said 'with' the festivals. רב ששת starts to explain that ברייתא, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only a sage can dissolve a vow
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: the words 'זה הדבר' teach that a חכם does התרה, but a בעל does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is the thing' teaches that a sage dissolves vows, but a husband does not dissolve them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא from the previous page. It says the words 'זה הדבר' limit the power of התרה to a חכם, so a husband cannot do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different powers over vows. One is הפרה, the husband cancelling his wife's vow. The other is התרה, a חכם releasing a vow. This ברייתא reads 'זה הדבר' as a limit, so the husband does not get the חכם's power of התרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage or halachic authority who can release vows
The husband
Dissolves or releases a vow (הַתָּרָה), usually after looking for an opening of regret

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two verbs apart. מתיר (releasing) is what a חכם does, and מפר (cancelling) is what a husband does. The whole passage depends on not mixing them up.

phrases.english: "This is the thing"
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:2. This line is the end of a ברייתא that started on the previous page.

phrases.english: a sage dissolves, but a husband does not dissolve.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַדָּבָר — חָכָם מַתִּיר, וְאֵין בַּעַל מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a חכם can do התרה; a בעל cannot.

steps.title: A second teaching: only a husband can cancel a vow
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא reads 'זה הדבר' in the other direction: a בעל does הפרה, but a חכם does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'This is the thing' means a husband cancels vows, but a sage does not cancel them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that uses the same words, 'זה הדבר', to limit the husband's power of הפרה to the husband alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא kept the בעל out of the חכם's power. This one keeps the חכם out of the בעל's power. Together they show the two powers are completely separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels a vow (הֲפָרָה), as a husband or father does

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches: "This is the thing"
a husband cancels, but a sage does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: זֶה הַדָּבָר — בַּעַל מֵפֵר וְאֵין חָכָם מֵפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ברייתא that reads the same words in the opposite direction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a בעל can do הפרה; a חכם cannot.

steps.title: Why a verse is needed: a tempting logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that without the verse, a קל וחומר would have given the חכם the power of הפרה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one might have thought: if a husband, who cannot dissolve, can still cancel, then surely a sage, who can dissolve, should be able to cancel!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lays out the logic that the verse has to block. It sets up a קל וחומר that seems to give the חכם the husband's power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument runs from weaker to stronger. The husband is the 'weaker' one, since he cannot do התרה, and yet he can do הפרה. So the חכם, who is 'stronger' because he can do התרה, should surely be able to do הפרה too. This explains why the ברייתא needed a verse in Step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: For one might have thought
Just as… (the opening of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר argument)
Is it not logical? (a rhetorical 'surely')

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיָּכוֹל: וּמָה בַּעַל שֶׁאֵין מַתִּיר — מֵפֵר,
phrases.english: For one might have thought: just as a husband, who does not dissolve, still cancels,
a sage, who does dissolve, is it not logical that he cancels?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל: וּמָה בַּעַל שֶׁאֵין מַתִּיר — מֵפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the need for the derivation in Step 2 by presenting the opposing קל וחומר
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a חכם cannot do הפרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the husband lacks התרה yet has הפרה, so the חכם, who has התרה, should surely have הפרה too.

steps.title: The verse blocks the logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'זה הדבר' overrides the קל וחומר and keeps הפרה for the husband alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse says 'This is the thing': a husband cancels, but a sage does not cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר by pointing to the verse. The verse limits הפרה to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would have given the חכם the power of הפרה, but the Torah's wording 'זה הדבר' says exactly this way and no other. The ברייתא repeats the rule from Step 2 on purpose, to close off the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (used when a verse overrides a logical argument)

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות together: only a חכם does התרה, only a בעל does הפרה. Each power belongs to one person only.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "This is the thing"
a husband cancels, but a sage does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: זֶה הַדָּבָר — בַּעַל מֵפֵר, וְאֵין חָכָם מֵפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קל וחומר of Step 3 with a verse
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation overrides a logical derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר, a חכם should also be able to do הפרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'זה הדבר' limit הפרה to the בעל.

steps.title: Linking vows and slaughtering outside the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on 'זה הדבר' teaches that פרשת נדרים, like שחוטי חוץ, is addressed to אהרן, his sons and all Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'This is the thing', and it says elsewhere 'This is the thing' about slaughtering outside the Temple. Just as that section is addressed to אהרן, his sons and all Israel, so too the section of vows is addressed to אהרן, his sons and all Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching links two sections of the Torah that both use the words 'זה הדבר'. It moves the audience of the שחוטי חוץ section over to the vows section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vows section is spoken to 'ראשי המטות', while the שחוטי חוץ section is spoken to 'אהרן, his sons and all Israel'. Through the גזירה שוה, the vows section borrows that wider audience. The גמרא will soon ask what practical law this teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two verses that share the same words, so that a law moves from one to the other
Offerings slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
It says here… and it says elsewhere (the opening of a גזירה שוה)
The section of the Torah about vows

phrases.english: It is stated here "This is the thing,"
and it is stated elsewhere "This is the thing" about offerings slaughtered outside.
Just as with offerings slaughtered outside,
it is Aaron and his sons and all Israel,
so too the section of vows
is Aaron and his sons and all Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן זֶה הַדָּבָר, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן זֶה הַדָּבָר בִּשְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ברייתא that uses the same words, 'זה הדבר', for a different derivation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פרשת נדרים is addressed to אהרן, his sons and all Israel, like שחוטי חוץ.

steps.title: The link works in the other direction too
steps.stepSummary: The same גזירה שוה moves 'ראשי המטות' from the vows section over to שחוטי חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as here it says 'the heads of the tribes', so too there it means 'the heads of the tribes'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the two-way link: the שחוטי חוץ section now borrows the 'ראשי המטות' from the vows section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each section gives the other what it has. Vows got 'all Israel', and שחוטי חוץ gets 'ראשי המטות'. This sets up the גמרא's two questions about what each borrowed detail teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The heads of the tribes (במדבר 30:2)

phrases.english: And just as here it is the heads of the tribes,
so too there it is the heads of the tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה כָּאן רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת — אַף לְהַלָּן רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-way גזירה שוה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחוטי חוץ is also connected to 'ראשי המטות'.

steps.title: What practical law does the vows side teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law comes from applying 'all Israel' to פרשת נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the section of vows, for what law is this taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes that the vows section is addressed to all Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה must teach some real law. So the גמרא wants to know what changes in the laws of vows once 'all Israel' is included.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: In the section of vows, for what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפָרָשַׁת נְדָרִים לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of Step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law comes from addressing פרשת נדרים to all Israel

steps.title: Three ordinary people can release a vow
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב: the link teaches that three הדיוטות are able to do התרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: to allow three ordinary people to release vows.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that 'all Israel' teaches that releasing a vow does not need a great sage. Three ordinary people are enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the section is addressed to all Israel and not only to leaders, regular people also have a role in התרה. A group of three ordinary people can do it.

keyTerms.meaning: To make valid or qualified
Ordinary people who are not expert sages

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
To qualify three ordinary people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לְהַכְשִׁיר שְׁלֹשָׁה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7

steps.title: But the verse says 'heads of the tribes'!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the verse speaks of ראשי המטות, which sounds like leaders, not ordinary people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'the heads of the tribes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אחא בר יעקב. The verse itself mentions leaders, so how can ordinary people qualify?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ordinary people can release vows, then the words 'ראשי המטות' seem to have no purpose. The challenge is that this part of the verse would be left unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written…? (a challenge from a verse)

phrases.english: But "the heads of the tribes" is written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's ruling that three הדיוטות qualify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse names leaders, which seems to contradict giving ordinary people this power.

steps.title: 'Heads of the tribes' teaches about a single expert
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (or רבי יוחנן): 'ראשי המטות' teaches that one expert alone can release a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said, and some say רבי יוחנן: it refers to a single expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'ראשי המטות' has its own job. It teaches that one expert sage alone can release a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both parts of the verse are used. 'All Israel' teaches that three ordinary people can do התרה, and 'ראשי המטות' teaches that a single expert can do it alone. The two methods do not conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: A single expert sage

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to release a vow: three ordinary people (from 'all Israel') or one expert (from 'ראשי המטות').

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said, and some say Rabbi Yochanan:
With a single expert.
phrases.notes: He means the words 'heads of the tribes' teach that one expert alone can release a vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּיָחִיד מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the challenging phrase its own separate law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ראשי המטות' seems to exclude ordinary people.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ראשי המטות' teaches that a יחיד מומחה can do התרה alone, alongside three הדיוטות.

steps.title: What does the other side of the link teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law comes from applying 'ראשי המטות' to שחוטי חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The heads of the tribes' regarding slaughtering outside the Temple, for what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question about the other direction of the link from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to see what 'heads of the tribes', the people who release vows, has to do with offerings slaughtered outside the Temple. The גמרא wants the practical law.

phrases.english: The heads of the tribes regarding offerings slaughtered outside,
for what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת בִּשְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question to Step 7, about the second direction of the גזירה שוה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law comes from linking 'ראשי המטות' to שחוטי חוץ

steps.title: Consecrating can be undone through a sage
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת: the link teaches that שאלה (asking a sage for release) works on הקדש too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: to teach that there is release by request for consecrated property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that the link teaches that a person who consecrated something can ask a sage to undo it, just like a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ראשי המטות' are the people who release vows. Moving them into the section about offerings shows that their power reaches הקדש as well. So a regretted consecration can be undone through שאלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a sage to release a vow or commitment
Property consecrated to the Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that consecrating property is treated like a vow, so a sage can undo it.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
To say that there is release by request for consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁאֵלָה בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11

steps.title: What does the link teach according to בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold there is no שאלה on הקדש. So the reason רב ששת gave for applying 'ראשי המטות' to שחוטי חוץ cannot work for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בית שמאי, who say there is no asking for release on הקדש, what law do we learn by reading 'ראשי המטות' as if it were written about שחוטי חוץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב ששת's answer does not work for בית שמאי, because they say a sage cannot release הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, רב ששת said the link teaches that שאלה works on הקדש. בית שמאי hold the opposite, that there is no שאלה on הקדש. So for them, the link between 'ראשי המטות' and שחוטי חוץ seems to teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי; they often disagree with בית הלל
Asking a sage to undo a vow or a consecration
Property set aside for the בית המקדש
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the courtyard of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: According to בית שמאי, who say
there is no asking for release on consecrated property,
'the heads of the tribes', treated as written about slaughtering outside,
phrases.notes: 'ראשי המטות' is really in the section on vows (במדבר 30:2). The link reads it as if it were also written about שחוטי חוץ.

phrases.english: what law does it teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי דְּאָמַר אֵין שְׁאֵלָה בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב ששת's answer against the opinion of בית שמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the link between נדרים and שחוטי חוץ according to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the link teaches that שאלה works on הקדש, and בית שמאי reject that law, then for them the link has no purpose.

steps.title: בית שמאי do not accept this גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי simply do not use the link between the two sections at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי do not hold of this גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the question does not start, because בית שמאי never accepted the link in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to find a law that the link teaches for בית שמאי, because they do not make the link at all. This answer creates new questions, which the next steps take up.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two places in the תורה that use the same word, so the laws of one apply to the other
They do not hold of it

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה.
phrases.english: בית שמאי do not have the verbal analogy.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by denying that בית שמאי use the link
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise: the link does not exist for בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone accepts the גזירה שוה and only argues about what it teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי do not use this גזירה שוה at all.

steps.title: Why is 'זה הדבר' written in the section on vows?
steps.stepSummary: If בית שמאי do not use the link, the words 'זה הדבר' in the section on vows need a purpose of their own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then what is 'זה הדבר' in the section on vows written for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'זה הדבר' teaches for בית שמאי, since they do not use it for the link. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For everyone else, the words 'זה הדבר' serve to build the link. Without the link, the גמרא assumes the words must still teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the thing', the shared words that make the link
The section of the תורה about vows (במדבר 30)

phrases.english: 'This is the thing' in the section on vows,
what is it written for?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זֶה הַדָּבָר״ בְּפָרָשַׁת נְדָרִים לְמַאי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 14: without the link, what is the phrase for?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of 'זה הדבר' in the section on vows according to בית שמאי

steps.title: A sage releases and a husband cancels
steps.stepSummary: 'זה הדבר' teaches that each one has only his own power: the sage does התרה, and the husband does הפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to say: a sage releases a vow, but a husband does not release it. A husband cancels a vow, but a sage does not cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'זה הדבר' marks the exact way each person deals with a vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different tools for vows. A חכם does התרה, which undoes the vow from the start. A husband does הפרה, which cancels his wife's vow from now on. 'זה הדבר' teaches that each one must use only his own tool and cannot use the other's.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage releases a vow (התרה)
A husband cancels his wife's vow (הפרה)

steps.confusionAlert: מתיר and מפר are not the same thing. מתיר is the sage's release, and מפר is the husband's cancellation. The point here is that they cannot be swapped.

phrases.english: To say: a sage releases,
but a husband does not release;
a husband cancels, but a sage does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר: חָכָם מַתִּיר וְאֵין בַּעַל מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זה הדבר' in the section on vows separates the sage's התרה from the husband's הפרה.

steps.title: Why is 'זה הדבר' written about שחוטי חוץ?
steps.stepSummary: The same question is now asked about 'זה הדבר' in the section on slaughtering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'זה הדבר' about slaughtering outside written for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about the other side of the link. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זה הדבר' also appear in the section on שחוטי חוץ. Without the link, בית שמאי need a separate purpose for them too.

phrases.english: 'This is the thing' about slaughtering outside,
what is it written for?

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זֶה הַדָּבָר״ בִּשְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ לְמַאי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15, now for the second section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of 'זה הדבר' in the section on שחוטי חוץ according to בית שמאי

steps.title: Liable for slaughtering, not for pinching
steps.stepSummary: 'זה הדבר' limits the punishment for שחוטי חוץ to שחיטה, and not to מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to say: one is liable for slaughtering outside, but one is not liable for pinching a bird's neck outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'זה הדבר' narrows the law of שחוטי חוץ to real slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זה הדבר' means 'this exact thing', so only שחיטה outside brings liability. מליקה is how a bird קרבן is killed inside the בית המקדש, but doing it outside does not bring this punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering with a knife
Pinching the back of a bird's neck with the כהן's fingernail, the way bird קרבנות are killed
Liable for punishment

steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, each 'זה הדבר' teaches its own local law: in נדרים it separates התרה from הפרה, and in שחוטי חוץ it limits liability to שחיטה.

phrases.english: To say: for slaughtering one is liable,
but one is not liable for pinching.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר: עַל הַשְּׁחִיטָה חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'זה הדבר' in שחוטי חוץ teaches liability for שחיטה but not for מליקה.

steps.title: Where do בית שמאי learn that three הדיוטות can release?
steps.stepSummary: Without the link, בית שמאי lose the source from step 8 that three הדיוטות can release a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to בית שמאי, where do we learn that three ordinary people are fit to release vows?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: if בית שמאי reject the link, they are missing the source for the law of three הדיוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, רב אחא בר יעקב learned from the link that three הדיוטות can release a vow. Since בית שמאי do not use the link, the גמרא asks where they get this law from.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary people, not expert sages
To make fit, to allow them
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: But according to בית שמאי,
from where do we know to allow three ordinary people?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, לְהַכְשִׁיר שְׁלֹשָׁה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the law from step 8 and asks how בית שמאי reach it without the link
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for three הדיוטות according to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The law of three הדיוטות came from the link, and בית שמאי reject the link, so they seem to have no source for it.

steps.title: They learn it from רב אסי בר נתן
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn the law of three הדיוטות from a different source, the teaching connected to רב אסי בר נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from what was taught by רב אסי בר נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי have a different source for the law of three הדיוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself stays the same. Only the source changes: instead of the link, בית שמאי rely on the explanation רב ששת gave to רב אסי בר נתן. The next steps set up that story, and רב ששת's explanation itself continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn it out from

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a law can stay the same even when two opinions learn it from different פסוקים.

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִדְּרַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן.
phrases.english: They derive it from that of רב אסי בר נתן.
phrases.notes: They learn it from the answer רב ששת gave to רב אסי בר נתן, which the next lines tell.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִדְּרַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 with another source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source for the same law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the link, בית שמאי would have no source for three הדיוטות.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי learn it from the teaching of רב אסי בר נתן.

steps.title: The verse about משה declaring the festivals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'וידבר משה את מועדי ה׳ אל בני ישראל' as the start of בית שמאי's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And משה declared the festivals of ה׳ to בני ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that holds the other source mentioned in step 20. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק closes the festival section in פרשת אמור (ויקרא 23). The vows section is not there; it comes in במדבר, right after the festival section of פרשת פנחס. The ברייתא in the next step reads meaning into which topics were said 'with' the festivals and which were not.

keyTerms.meaning: The festivals of ה׳
As it is written

phrases.english: As it is written: “And Moshe declared the festivals of the Lord
to the children of Israel.”

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the source that step 20 pointed to.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי have a source for three הדיוטות that does not depend on the 'זה הדבר' link.

steps.title: The ברייתא: שבת and vows were not said with the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says שבת was not said together with the מועדים. בן עזאי says the vows section was not said together with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי says, 'The festivals were said, but שבת בראשית was not said with them.' בן עזאי says, 'The festivals were said, but the section of vows was not said with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as separating the festivals from שבת and from the vows section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי's line about vows is the part that matters for releasing a vow through three הדיוטות. The festivals need an expert court, since the court sets the calendar, and vows do not. The גמרא has not explained this yet. First it questions the ברייתא itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The weekly שבת, which recalls the days of Creation
The Torah section about vows (במדבר 30)
Were said

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'והתניא' is not an attack. It simply brings the ברייתא that is the source, and that is how this ברייתא is being used.

phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
“The festivals” were said,
but the Shabbat of Creation was not said with them.
Ben Azzai says: “The festivals” were said,
but the section of vows was not said with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק quoted in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The vows section is set apart from the festivals.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי and בן עזאי

steps.title: רב אסי בר נתן travels to ask רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר נתן found the ברייתא hard. He went to נהרדעא to ask רב ששת, did not find him, and followed him to מחוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי בר נתן had a difficulty with this ברייתא. He came to נהרדעא before רב ששת but did not find him there, so he followed him to מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up the questions רב אסי בר נתן is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been ruled yet. The story shows that the ברייתא seemed hard enough for him to chase down רב ששת from city to city.

keyTerms.meaning: He found it difficult
A ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
After him, following him

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ הָא מַתְנִיתָא.
phrases.english: Rav Asi bar Natan had a difficulty with this baraita.
He came to Neharde'a, before Rav Sheshet,
but he did not find him.
He went after him to Mechoza.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי בַּר נָתָן קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ הָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces someone who questions the ברייתא from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This step only sets up רב אסי בר נתן's questions.

steps.title: But שבת is written with the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי בר נתן asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי can say שבת was not said with the festivals, when the תורה does write שבת with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'The festivals of ה׳ were said, and שבת בראשית was not said with them? But שבת is written with them!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי בר נתן challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's line in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the festival sections, ויקרא 23 and במדבר 28, the Torah mentions שבת right alongside the festivals. So a plain reading of 'שבת was not said with them' seems to go against the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written!

phrases.english: He said to him: The festivals of the Lord were said,
and the Shabbat of Creation was not said with them?
But Shabbat is written with them!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the festivals: in their sections of the Torah, שבת shows up right alongside them (ויקרא 23:3; במדבר 28:9-10).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב שַׁבָּת עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first question רב אסי בר נתן brings to רב ששת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's claim in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים plainly list שבת together with the festivals.

steps.title: But the vows section is right next to the festivals
steps.stepSummary: He also challenges בן עזאי: the vows section appears right beside the festival section.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And further: the festivals of ה׳ were said, and the section of vows was not said with them? But it is written right beside them!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי בר נתן adds a second challenge, this time to בן עזאי's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vows section in במדבר 30 comes directly after the festival offerings in במדבר 28-29. So how can בן עזאי say vows were not said 'with' the festivals?

keyTerms.meaning: And further, and another point
From the side, right next to it

phrases.english: And further: The festivals of the Lord were said,
and the section of vows was not said with them?
But it is written right beside them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִסִּיטְרָא כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question, now aimed at בן עזאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's claim in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תורה, the vows section sits directly next to the festival section.

steps.title: רב ששת begins his explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers: 'This is what the ברייתא is teaching.' The explanation itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'This is what it teaches:'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts to answer. This line only opens his explanation, which comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'הכי קתני' means the ברייתא should not be read word for word. רב ששת will explain the point it is really making about how the festivals differ from שבת and from vows.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches, meaning: read it this way

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what it teaches:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רב ששת's answer to both questions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא (the details come next)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that שבת and vows are not written near the festivals at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come: רב ששת will explain what 'not said with them' really means.
